findings.title: QR mutation property does not enforce its stated successful-parse condition
findings.status: confirmed in source across all 20 selected heads; not a demonstrated production vulnerability
findings.confidence: High in static test logic; no runtime validation performed
findings.description: The multipart test names its property as rejection of a changed chunk or preservation of the same session. Its successful branch calls parseChunk but discards the return value and performs no session or protected-field assertion. Only thrown errors are checked. A future parser regression that accepts changed protected data could therefore pass this particular property. Separate deterministic CRC, conflict, size and final-integrity tests are present, so this does not establish that current production parsing accepts such data.
findings.impact_conditions: A future parser regression succeeds on a mutated input and the project relies on this property to verify the named successful-parse constraint. This affects verification assurance rather than an established current payment or signature bypass.
findings.remediation: Assert the intended invariant on every successful parse and keep the typed-error assertion on rejected input. Name the test according to the exact property it checks.
findings.non_operational_acceptance_criteria: A code review can trace every successful and failed branch to an explicit assertion of the named property; ordinary isolated unit assertions confirm a successful parse cannot skip the invariant check. No live target, oversized artifact or exploit recipe is needed.

evidence.role: Existing separate rejection/integrity assertions limit the finding

findings.title: Development-key refusal depends on raw key spelling
findings.status: confirmed static validation mismatch across all original 20 selected heads; no deployment or runtime reproduction
findings.confidence: High for source-level mismatch; no deployed impact established
findings.description: The testnet deployment driver accepts more than one textual representation of a 32-byte signing key, but its explicit refusal of the known public development key compares the input with one raw string. The spelling check does not establish that the effective signing key is different. The keystore branch also does not inspect signer identity. The documented rejection is therefore narrower than the accepted signer representations.
findings.impact_conditions: An operator explicitly enables a supported public-testnet broadcast and supplies the public development signer in an accepted representation or via a keystore. A mistakenly funded publicly known signer would remain publicly controllable. This helper accepts only the listed testnets; this review does not establish a mainnet deployment path or an active Pages wallet/payment vulnerability.
findings.remediation: Apply the development-signer restriction to the effective signer identity for both raw-key and keystore paths. Normalize and validate key bytes before equality decisions, and check the derived public address before signing. Preserve explicit broadcast confirmation.
findings.non_operational_acceptance_criteria: Source review shows that all accepted raw-key representations and all signer-selection paths reach the same identity check before a broadcast operation. Future isolated fixture tests can assert identity equivalence without loading a funded account, connecting to RPC or sending transactions.

evidence.role: Supported network restriction limits assessed exposure to testnet deployment tooling

findings.title: Rehearsal cleanup can remove earlier deployment records
findings.status: confirmed static cleanup scope across all original 20 selected heads; no files deleted or reproduction executed
findings.confidence: High for source-level file selection; no actual historical record loss established
findings.description: Before a local rehearsal, the driver refuses only when run-latest.json already exists. Its EXIT cleanup removes every regular file at the top level of the selected chain broadcast directory. Pre-existing timestamped or otherwise retained deployment records can exist without run-latest.json and are consequently within the cleanup selection even though the rehearsal did not create them. Cleanup also runs after a failed rehearsal.
findings.impact_conditions: The operator invokes rehearsal while the chain-specific broadcast directory contains earlier regular files and no run-latest.json. This can remove local deployment provenance and recovery information. It does not delete blockchain state or directly move user funds.
findings.remediation: Give rehearsal an isolated temporary broadcast and cache destination, then remove only that owned directory. If tool constraints require a shared destination, record its initial contents and remove only files created by the current operation; never sweep all pre-existing top-level records.
findings.non_operational_acceptance_criteria: A static ownership check shows cleanup confined to a newly allocated rehearsal directory. An isolated temporary-file fixture may confirm that a pre-existing sentinel record remains byte-for-byte unchanged after both success and failure cleanup, without running a node, deploying a contract or using a real broadcast directory.

evidence.role: Rehearsal reuses the normal broadcast location before cleanup
